title: August Inflation US - Annual
description:
This is a market about inflation over the 12-month period ending August 2026, before seasonal adjustment, as reported by the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

This market will resolve to the percentage change in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) over the 12-month period ending in August 2026 according to the monthly Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) report.

The resolution source for this market will be the BLS Consumer Price Index report released for August 2026 (https://www.bls.gov/bls/news-release/cpi.htm), currently scheduled to be released on September 11, 2026, at 8:30 AM ET. Resolution of this market will take place upon release of the aforementioned data.

Note: the resolution source for this market will be the official monthly BLS CPI news release, which reports inflation over 12-month periods to only one decimal point (e.g., 2.9%). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

If the BLS does not release the relevant figures on the scheduled date, this market may remain open up until the scheduled release time of the next CPI report (https://www.bls.gov/schedule). If the information is not released by that time, this market will resolve according to the figures of the most recent previous month with available data.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Market-implied odds center on 3.3–3.4% for August 2026 headline CPI year-over-year, reflecting July’s 3.4% print and forecasts for a modest 0.2–0.4% month-over-month rise.** Persistent energy prices, shelter costs, and supercore services inflation continue to anchor readings near current levels, while AI-related demand pressures on goods and software add upside risks. Recent July data showed core CPI at 2.5% year-over-year, with gasoline and food components rebounding modestly per analyst estimates. Traders are weighting the balance between cooling goods prices and sticky services, with the September 11 release serving as the immediate catalyst. The distribution around 3.3–3.5% captures uncertainty over whether month-over-month momentum will hold or ease slightly from July’s pace.
